title: Contrast-adaptive token scale and micro-shadow tiling for high-density components
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Scope: Introduce a contrast-adaptive token scale (color ramps + type delta) together with a micro-shadow tiling approach to reduce visual noise and rendering cost in dense UIs (tables, compact cards, chart overlays). This work produces a small, composable token set and a migration/adoption playbook for components and charts. Goals: 1) improve legibility at small sizes and high density, 2) reduce apparent visual clutter from overlapping shadows, 3) provide deterministic fallbacks for low-contrast contexts (e.g., blur, low-brightness), and 4) create developer-friendly token aliases for rapid adoption.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 contrast-adaptive neutral ramps (low/medium/high density) with usage guidelines for body, caption, and muted states.
Ship variable type deltas (small/compact/regular) with example tokens and CSS variables for scale interpolation.
Introduce micro-shadow-tiling tokens (tile-1..tile-4) and document rendering recommendations to avoid double-shadowing in stacked elements.
Update button, table row, and chart tooltip components to consume new tokens in a feature-flagged rollout.
Provide 10 representative migration examples (PRs or design patches) with before/after images and performance notes.
Add automated visual regression tests for 12 density/contrast permutations.
Document accessibility rationale and include contrast measurements versus WCAG guidelines for each token usage example.
design_notes: Rationale: Traditional single-scale neutral ramps produce insufficient contrast at 11px/12px caption sizes in dense tables. We computed color deltas that are perceptually linear at small sizes and tuned for typical dashboard backdrops.

Shadow tiling: Instead of a single heavier shadow for stacked cards/rows, the tiling tokens use thinner layered shadows with reduced blur and vertical offsets to preserve depth cues while lowering cumulative alpha and GPU overdraw.

Token shape: Tokens will be introduced as semantic aliases (surface-default, surface-muted-dense, border-strong-dense, text-primary-compact). Implementation will expose CSS variables and JSON token files for runtime selection.

Chart overlays: Provide a recommended overlay palette that preserves mark visibility across background densities; include explicit alpha suggestions for area/fill marks to avoid muddying colors when multiple overlays stack.
Design files: initial spec in Figma (file: /Redwood/Design/Tokens/Contrast-Adapt-2025) with component page examples and knobbed density controls.
decisions: Adopt contrast-adaptive approach rather than forcing a single high-contrast ramp to preserve visual hierarchy in light and dark themes.
Implement shadow tiling tokens as the default for compact tables and compact cards; provide opt-out token for legacy appearance.
Expose tokens as semantic aliases (not raw hexs) to allow future remapping without component changes.
Require automated visual diff checks in the visual-testing pipeline for all token rollouts before unflagging.
